text:
marta: quick heads-up: deploybot auto-sticky-pinned runtime-3.8 after a flurry of OOMs on the 'transform-lite' family. We need a plan for a scoped unpin + decay policy in the 01:00 UTC change window.

deploybot: [automated] sticky pin applied. pin_id=pb-2025-09-17-77. Affected: model-group 'transform-lite' (transform-small, transform-lite). Trigger: OOMs > 3% over 10m. See https://redwood.internal/pins/pb-2025-09-17-77 for details.

oliver: quick telemetry note: errors spike on long-seq batch jobs and a couple of nightly pipelines. Interactive short queries unaffected.

taylor: proposal: scoped unpin that excludes hosts with label `tenant:dedicated` and limits traffic to max_seq<=4096 and batch_size<=8. Do canary in us-east first. Also propose sticky->soft decay: sticky -> soft after 4h if signals improve; soft auto-unpin after 24h if stable.

marta: sounds reasonable. Ops: can deploybot schedule a scoped canary unpin and convert sticky->soft automatically based on thresholds?

ops-sre-bot: runbook section updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pinning. Example commands below. Deploybot supports scoped unpin + decay rules in the same operation. Monitored signals: `oom_rate`, `crash_rate`, `p95_latency`.

# Suggested sequence (short):
# 1) label canary hosts: pin_canary=pb-2025-09-17-77
# 2) canary scoped unpin (us-east, exclude dedicated):
#    deploybot unpin --pin pb-2025-09-17-77 --scope region:us-east \
#      --traffic-filter "max_seq<=4096 AND batch_size<=8 AND tenant:!=dedicated" \
#      --mode canary --tag-header "X-Canary-Pin:pb-2025-09-17-77"
# 3) monitor 20m: oom_rate, crash_rate, p95_latency + synthetic tests
# 4) decision point -> expand or rollback

oliver: rollback criteria idea: within 20m of canary, rollback if oom_rate > 0.6% OR crash_rate increases by >1pp OR p95 latency > baseline * 1.2. If partial instability, route affected short traffic to runtime-3.7.

taylor: i'll own canary and decision. i'll also add a short eval script that hits deterministic routes and checks model hash outputs.

marta: release notes: short blurb referencing pb-2025-09-17-77, affected models, and the scoped canary plan. @taylor please update the release tracker and ping CS.

ops-sre-bot: ops checklist (to run at 01:00 UTC):
1) tag canary hosts: `pin_canary=pb-2025-09-17-77`
2) run scoped canary unpin command above
3) run taylor's synthetic and monitor signals for 20m
4) decision at +20m -> expand to region:*, traffic-filter max_seq<=8192 OR rollback via `deploybot pin --pin pb-2025-09-17-77 --force`

taylor: synthetic sanity script (short):
```bash
for i in {1..300}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Canary-Pin: pb-2025-09-17-77" \
    "https://canary-east/api/generate?model=transform-lite&max_seq=1024&batch_size=4" > out.$i.json &
done
wait
jq -s '[.[]] | {errors: map(select(.status!=200))|length, p95: (map(.latency)|sort)[int(length*0.95)]}' out.*.json
```

oliver: i'll monitor infra traces and post any anomalies. if we hit noisy batch failure, we should consider a temporary route-level throttle as a mitigation.

marta: deploybot, can you schedule the canary for 01:00 UTC and wait for this channel ack? react with :eyes: to confirm.

deploybot: ready to schedule. React to acknowledge.

marta: ack. :eyes:

taylor: approved - will be on call for the window and will push updates here.

ops-sre-bot: tagging oncall rotation: primary @taylor, secondary @oliver. I will open a short incident note and add the pin id.

marta: thanks team. Keep this thread updated with canary results; if rollback happens, include the exact `deploybot pin --pin ... --force` command used and paste brief metrics snapshot.
